evidence: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125-131 passes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group. The semantic mismatch is real: legacy box-ordinal-group defaults to 1 and only accepts values >= 1, while modern `order` defaults to 0. So a generic mixin should emit $val + 1 for the legacy properties (the usual Bourbon/Compass approach). But the claimed mis-ordering does not happen with this PR's call sites. The only usages are order(3) on .panel (header.scss:39) and order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper (topic.scss:30). Their siblings keep the default (0 modern, 1 legacy), so 2 and 3 sort after the defaults and in the same relative order under both models. Divergence would only show up for order(1), which ties with defaults in legacy but sorts after them in modern, or for 0 or negative values. None of those are used. The legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box syntax also only applies to very old browsers, because the later `display: flex` wins in modern ones. Hardening the mixin with $val + 1 is a cheap safeguard for the future but not a bug today.
